definitions.gloss: to lament; to grieve; to bewail
definitions.explanation: To feel deep sadness or sorrow about something, or to express that grief. Often used for mourning a loss or deploring a situation.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}は{友人|ゆうじん}の{死|し}を{深|ふか}く{嘆|なげ}いた。
examples.english: He deeply mourned the death of his friend.

examples.japanese: {若者|わかもの}の{活字離|かつじばな}れを{嘆|なげ}く{声|こえ}が{多|おお}いが、{読書|どくしょ}の{形|かたち}が{変|か}わっただけかもしれない。
examples.english: Many voices lament young people's disinterest in print, but perhaps the form of reading has simply changed.

notes:
Can be written as either {嘆|なげ}く or {歎|なげ}く, though the first is far more common. Used both for personal grief and for deploring social trends or conditions. Has a literary quality and is often seen in written text.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
・{運命|うんめい}を{嘆|なげ}く: to lament one's fate
・{死|し}を{嘆|なげ}く: to mourn a death
・{嘆|なげ}き{悲|かな}しむ: to grieve and sorrow
・{世|よ}を{嘆|なげ}く: to lament the state of the world
